Why not Common.File?  I don't see a reason to make a new top-level directory for one interface and ".Object" isn't really a useful part of the name.
Done

This interface appears to capture details specific to the PLDM specification, while also attempting to generalize its usage for any file on the BMC. This is problematic, as we currently lack documentation or a design that explains how applications other than PLDM could leverage this interface to expose arbitrary files over D-Bus.

For example, the concept of exclusivity in the context of `DfOpen()` is clear within PLDM, but its applicability to generic files on the BMC is unclear. Similarly, the `PurposeType` field does not seem to align well when applied to arbitrary files outside PLDM’s scope.

In my view, it would be better to scope this as an interface within the PLDM namespace for now. Once we have a well-defined design that addresses how other applications could use this interface, we can revisit making it more broadly applicable.

Indeed, PLDM is the only current target in my mind to host this interface. I'm Okay with either placing it in Common/ or PLDM/.

Putting it under PLDM/ will require future consumers of this interface to be aware that they are retrieving files via PLDM. However, as the intended purpose for this interface is for BMC to retrieve system dump and the interaction between BMC and Host/remote entities might need to be OEM-defined, that awareness can inevitably be involved.

I would let @patrick@stwcx.xyz take a call on this one. I am leaning towards this being in the PLDM namespace. Since there is no design that talks about how any arbitrary application can use this interface at the moment.
IMO `xyz.openbmc_project.PLDM.File`; +1 to @manojkiran.eda@gmail.com's concern. Any attempt at a common interface needs to strip out all the PLDM-isms.

What does this mean?  How does the file get "released" from this state?

A file may allow multiple sessions opened to it. An exclusive session preserves consistent file content (avoid modification from other sessions or the host of the file) while this session is open. This can be released when Read() returns (if the implementation returns a memfd), or after the server side finishes writing to the fd it returned to the clients through Read() (in case of streaming data through a normal unix socket or socketpair).
Resolved. Please re-open if necessary.

Is this something that comes from PLDM specifically?  If so, how does it map to other interfaces?  We don't want a PLDM-ism reflected on dbus and we don't want it in a "common" interface.

It's initially from PLDM spec which classifies File Descriptor PDR. We want to use this file interface to retrieve computer system diagnostic data via Redfish `LogServices/Dump/CollectDiagnosticData` action so there needs to be a scheme to tell that this is a diagnostic data on D-Bus and its type is <Purpose>.

However, `DiagnosticDataType` property passed into `CollectDiagnosticData` action only has {CPER, CPERSection, Manager, OEM, OS, PreOS}, so the `OEMDiagnosticDataType` can be filled in to specify what kind of OEM diagnostic data users want to collect and it can be then mapped to <Purpose>.

Is parent path same as PLDM terminus or same as directory? How are duplicate filenames to be handled? Is there a restriction on the length of the filename - is this the actual filename or some other ID? Not all typical file name characters may be allowed on a D-Bus pathname.

> Is parent path same as PLDM terminus or same as directory?

<ParentPath> is the director name from the PLDM File PDRs.

> How are duplicate filenames to be handled?

In the other thread we are discussing about using:
`xyz/openbmc_project/file/<terminus_name>/<Some_folder_name>/<FileName>` or `/xyz/openbmc_project/file/[<ParentPath>]/<FileName>`.

I think adding <terminus_name> as root path of one terminus will be better solution. This approach will handle the duplication of filenames.

> Is there a restriction on the length of the filename - is this the actual filename or some other ID?

File name is just file name from PDRs. As the sensors name we don't expect to use `ID` in the file name.
Because the file name completely from the File PDRs, as the define of `FileName` field in the File PDRs, the filename is string ASCII `characters are
encoded using the 8-bit ISO8859-1 "ASCII + Latin1" character set encoding` and max length is 256. 

> Not all typical file name characters may be allowed on a D-Bus pathname.

Yes, it just the same as sensor name object paths.

> Is parent path same as PLDM terminus or same as directory

It's a generic term to cover any directory name ahead of this file if exists.

> How are duplicate filenames to be handled? Is there a restriction on the length of the filename - is this the actual filename or some other ID? Not all typical file name characters may be allowed on a D-Bus pathname.

If we talk about PLDM File Transfer, the <FileName> is a trimmed version from FileName field in File Descriptor PDR. The spec says `This shall be a unique file name (for the device)`, so for PLDM File Transfer, the topmost parent directory of any file will be its terminus name. Therefore, it's guaranteed from the spec perspective that no duplication is encountered. Please search for "Proposed file object path hierarchy" in https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/76960.

And as it's a trimmed version, all invalid characters in the FileName field will be replaced by underscores just like how other apps do.
